subject: Customer data access gating questions and actions
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Novak <elena@novabanking.com>
Cc: NovaBank Security <security@novabanking.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Customer data access gating questions and actions

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can move to a short technical qualification: 

- Scope we discussed: real-time transaction enrichment (PII present in input), embeddings for internal search, and short-term log storage for debugging (30 days).
- Primary asks from your security team: data residency in us-east-1, SOC 2 evidence, and a support access model (RBAC + break-glass flow) with audit logging.

Can you confirm the following so we can map with our product controls: 
1) Is NovaBank comfortable with a model where primary data stays in your VPC and only token metadata/pseudonymized telemetry leaves the VPC for hosted telemetry?
2) Data retention ceiling: you mentioned 30 days for logs — is that strict regulatory requirement or negotiable for debug traces?
3) For support access: do you require JIT (time-boxed) elevated access with customer approval, or is a pre-authorized small group acceptable? We can propose both flows.

If you can attach your SOC 2 summary and the retention spreadsheet you referenced, that would be helpful. Next steps on our side: I'll route the answers to our security/product folks for a short qualification and draft a proposed JIT break-glass runbook for your review.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Elena Novak <elena@novabanking.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Customer data access gating questions and actions

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. See answers below and attached files (SOC2 summary and retention spreadsheet).

1) Residency: must remain in AWS us-east-1 (we cannot permit egress of raw PII to other regions). Pseudonymized telemetry that cannot be tied back to a client ID is acceptable to flow out for cost/ops analytics.
2) Retention: logs containing transaction IDs must be retained for 30 days; anonymized debug traces can be kept for up to 90 days. This is a regulatory constraint for our fraud ops.
3) Support access: preference is JIT with secondary approver (security manager) for any elevated access. Pre-authorized permanent elevated accounts are not acceptable for production systems.

Attachments: NovaBank_SOC2_summary.pdf, NovaBank_Data_Retention_Reqs.xlsx

We can also share a short redline on an access policy template if that helps. Happy to take a follow-up call next week with your security team.

Elena Novak
Head of Platform Security, NovaBank
elena@novabanking.com

Folks — forwarding NovaBank's answers and attachments (SOC2 + retention sheet). Summary of asks: us-east-1 residency for PII, 30d retention hardline for logs with 90d for anonymized traces, and JIT + secondary approver for support break-glass.

Can we qualify whether Redwood Hosted (private VPC peering option) can meet these constraints with our current platform controls? Specific asks: 
- Feasibility: keep raw PII in customer VPC while allowing pseudonymized telemetry out.
- Support access flow: propose a JIT break-glass that creates timeboxed IAM role, requires two-step approval (engineer request + security manager approve), and logs to immutable audit log. Include estimated implementation risk and timeline.
- Cost/ops impact: any additional egress or logging costs we should flag to the AE for the deal.

Elena is open to a joint call with security. Ideally have a one-page JIT proposal we can send to them before scheduling. I attached the two files they sent and a placeholder for a short runbook draft (redwood-jit-breakglass-proposal.pdf).

Thanks —
Vanessa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, ben.carter@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Customer data access gating questions and actions

Thanks for the context — quick technical qualification below. High level: this is implementable with Redwood Private deployed into NovaBank's VPC + a hybrid telemetry sink. Details and proposed next steps: 

- Residency: we can ensure raw PII never leaves the customer's VPC by deploying a Private control plane with peered inference workers in their us-east-1 account. All model compute and I/O to ephemeral storage stays in VPC.
- Telemetry: propose a local collector that strips direct identifiers, hashes stable IDs with customer-provided salt, and forwards only pseudonymized metrics to our hosted analytics in us-east-1. We will provide schema and hashing proof.
- Retention: platform supports configurable retention per artifact. We can set logs with TTL 30d for transaction logs and 90d for anonymized traces; retention enforced by lifecycle policies in S3 buckets in the customer's account.
- Support access / JIT break-glass: implement timeboxed IAM role creation with automatic revoke. Flow: engineer requests via console -> security manager approval (out-of-band email or ticket) -> short-lived role (1 hour) created with just-in-time permissions + session recording. All access events are sent to immutable audit S3 and a write-once log (WORM) if required. We also log keystrokes/commands for support sessions if customer opts in.

Risks & notes: if NovaBank requires cryptographic separation (HSM-backed key control) for hashing, we'll need their KMS in the VPC; that adds approx 2-3 weeks integration effort. Implementing WORM logs may require elevated retention settings and an estimate of ~$2k/month depending on volume.

Action items I propose:
1) I will draft a 1-pager JIT break-glass runbook and a short architecture diagram for NovaBank by EOD tomorrow.
2) Ben, can you prep an initial cost delta for running Private in their account + telemetry pipeline?
3) Priyom, please flag any compliance docs we should send upfront (SOC2 artifacts, encryption proof).

If this looks good, Vanessa, let's send the 1-pager and schedule a 30-min follow-up with Elena + their security manager next week.

Karthik
Director, Product Security, Redwood Inference
